text:
Erin: Quick RFC follow-up — we need to decide on the canonical MHA memory layout for the runtime. Two axes: NHWC vs NCHW ordering, and contiguous QKV (interleaved in a single buffer) vs separate Q/K/V tensors. Thoughts on kernel selection complexity and runtime routing?

Mike: +1 to hashing this out. Short summary of tradeoffs as I see it: contiguous QKV -> allows a single fused kernel for matmul + softmax + output proj, fewer passes over memory. Separate Q/K/V -> simpler KV cache interface and easier to change quantization per tensor.

Sophia: Also consider stride implications. If we pick NHWC (batch, seq, head, head_dim) we get contiguous head_dim which is nice for GEMM inner loops. NCHW-like (batch, head, seq, head_dim) favors different transposes. Cache friendliness depends on which axis we iterate.

Ravi: Practical constraint: our KV cache currently assumes K and V are appended per step and stored as [batch, head, seq, head_dim]. Changing to a fused QKV buffer will force either copying into cache or awkward views with non-unit strides. That kills perf unless we update the cache API.

Alice: Proposed middle ground: keep KV cache separate but let inference kernels accept either separate or packed Q (i.e., Q packed with projection) so we only fuse where it helps. That means kernel selection based on a small layout enum at dispatch time.

Erin: Runtime dispatch concerns: checking layout enum per-call is cheap, but having 4+ specialized kernels increases maintenance burden. Would prefer a small set (generic + 2 fused) rather than per-layout-per-quant.

Mike: Agreed. Another point: alignment and padding. On CUDA/ROCm we want 64B alignment for loads. Interleaved QKV often introduces padding between heads to hit alignment which wastes memory but improves vector load efficiency. We should benchmark head_dim sizes 32/64/128 for padding breakpoints.

Sophia: Put a small snippet of the layouts for clarity:

```
// NHWC contiguous QKV (packed): [B, S, 3, H, D] contiguous as ...S,3,H,D
// Separate tensors: Q: [B, S, H, D], K: [B, S, H, D], V: [B, S, H, D]
// KV cache currently: [B, H, S_total, D] appended along S_total
```

Ravi: If we do packed QKV, appending to KV cache will require an extract/copy of K/V fields into the cache layout. That's extra memcpy per step. For streaming/auto-regressive workloads that kills throughput.

Alice: What about a hybrid buffer: store Q packed for immediate matmul, but maintain lightweight separate K/V views for cache append (zero-copy when possible). Might need to align memory and create strided views. Requires runtime support for non-contiguous tensors in kernels.

Erin: How complex would it be to teach the kernels to accept strided K/V views? Cost vs benefit? If kernels support arbitrary stride for the sequence axis we can avoid copies but increase kernel branching and maybe lose some vectorization.

Mike: We can implement two codepaths: optimized contiguous path (fast) and a fallback strided path (slower). Dispatcher picks based on is_contiguous. This is similar to what we do for quantized kernels. Perf delta needs measurement.

Sophia: Also note: hardware MATMUL libraries (cutlass, rocBLAS) prefer contiguous leading dims. If we handcraft kernels we can pack/transform inside the kernel (on-the-fly pack) which hides the copy from callers, but then kernel complexity rises.

Ravi: For small sequence lengths (chatty requests) copy overhead is small; for long-context or streaming it's large. So metrics should be seq_len-aware routing. Perhaps a policy: if seq_len < 64, pack on-demand; else require pre-packed separated K/V.

Alice: API implication: add a layout hint and a preferred_policy (e.g., auto/pack-if-short/require-separate) to the model config. That keeps runtime flexible and lets customers choose predictable behavior for Dedicated/Private.

Erin: I like that. Action items: 1) Sophia + Mike add microbench harness for: packed QKV vs separate, seq_len in {8,64,1024}, head_dim {32,64,128}, batch {1,8,64}. 2) Ravi to prototype strided-kernel fallback and measure penalty. 3) Alice to draft small API RFC for layout hint + policy.

Mike: I'll land bench scripts and share perf table link. Expecting big wins for packed at head_dim=64 with batch large.

Sophia: One more gotcha: quantization/INT8. Some packed formats (interleaving channels) make per-channel scales harder. If we allow mixed quant (Q int8, K/V fp16) layout must be explicit.

Ravi: Noted. We'll ensure benchmarks include mixed-precision variants.

deploy-bot: CI job started: runtime/mha-layout-bench (jobs/14322). Results will appear in the thread when complete. :gear:

Erin: Thanks everyone. If CI validates, Alice and I will merge the RFC stub and follow up with rollout plan (canary kernels -> telemetry -> enable-by-default).
